porta.name: Porta Four
porta.byline: This project's own design, after the four-track cassette recorders of 1979 onwards
facts: Four-track cassette recorder with a built-in mixer
The TEAC 144 Portastudio (1979) and the machines that followed it
about: The Porta Four is not a real product. It is drawn after the cassette four-tracks that began with the TEAC 144 Portastudio, launched in September 1979 at $899.

Before the Portastudio, recording more than one part meant booking a studio or buying an expensive open-reel machine. It put four tracks and a mixer onto an ordinary cassette, in a box that sat on a desk.
porta.significance: Home recording as an everyday thing starts with this kind of machine. Its limits, four tracks and a lot of tape hiss, became a sound people chose on purpose.

braun-tg60.name: Braun TG 60
facts: Two tracks in stereo; 9.5 and 19 cm/s
about: Braun's first tape recorder. Rams designed it to sit beside the company's hi-fi units, or to hang on the wall in a row with a control unit and two flat speakers, so every module shares the same height and depth.

Where other recorders hid their mechanism, this one shows it: exposed reels, a head plate with its screws on view, and a pressure roller that swings in as the tape starts. The keys are relay switches that respond to the lightest touch. Inside are three motors and three separate heads, the layout of a studio machine in a home appliance.
braun-tg60.significance: It is a design landmark more than a recording one. It shows the Braun idea that a machine's function can be its appearance, and it is collected and exhibited as an object: the photographs this version was drawn from were taken at the Pinakothek der Moderne in Munich.
braun-tg60.recordingsNote: No well-known recording is documented as made on a TG 60. It was a home hi-fi machine, bought to tape radio broadcasts and records.
braun-tg60.reproduction: About this version: drawn from museum photographs. The reel is shortened to three minutes, the amount of speed wobble is borrowed from Braun's later TG 1000, and what the "aus" key does is a guess.
